title: Aggregate with collections
summary: Count categories with a Map and choose the right collection for a report.

scenario.briefing: The campus report counts how many products belong to each category. The current code overwrites each count with 1. Accumulate the counts and keep the collection types explicit.

objectives.description: Accumulate counts in a typed map.
Choose a collection for a lookup-and-order requirement.
Explain map operations and collection behavior accurately.

hints: A HashMap lookup replaces the previous value when the key already exists.
Use Map.merge to add one to the existing count.
Integer::sum is a method reference that adds two integers.

misconceptions.description: Putting a literal 1 for every occurrence.
misconceptions.feedback: put replaces the previous count. merge adds the new occurrence to the existing value.

misconceptions.description: Using a bare list when lookup by key is required.
misconceptions.feedback: A list requires a scan for every lookup. A Map keyed by customer id gives direct access and can hold the orders in a list.

misconceptions.description: Expecting HashMap to preserve insertion order.
misconceptions.feedback: HashMap does not promise iteration order. Use LinkedHashMap when insertion order matters.

sections.title: Choose a collection for the access pattern
sections.body: A List keeps insertion order and allows duplicates. A Set rejects duplicates but does not promise order. A Map associates unique keys with values and supports constant-time lookup by key. Pick the structure from the operations the code performs, not from habit.

sections.title: Merge and compute update a map in one step
sections.body: Map.merge(key, value, remappingFunction) inserts the value when the key is absent and combines it when the key exists. For counting, merge(category, 1, Integer::sum) replaces a get, null-check, and put sequence.

sections.title: Streams compose transformations
sections.body: The stream API can filter, map, group, and collect without mutating the source. Collectors.groupingBy builds a map of lists. Use streams when the pipeline is clearer; use a loop when it is not.

vocabulary.definition: A collection of unique keys mapped to values.
A Map operation that inserts or combines the value for a key.
A lazy sequence of values processed by a pipeline of operations.
A collection whose contents cannot be changed after creation.

steps.title: Count each category
steps.prompt: Edit Main.java. countByCategory returns the number of occurrences of each category. Use Map.merge so repeated categories accumulate.

tests.description: The method keeps the typed list and map signature.

hints: The map starts empty and the loop visits every category.
Replace put with an operation that reads the old value.
merge inserts 1 for a new key and combines for an existing key.

localVerification.description: Compile and run Main.java with the JDK.

steps.title: Choose the report structure
steps.prompt: A report needs each customer's orders in insertion order and direct lookup by customer id. Which structure fits?

quiz.explanation: The map provides lookup by customer id, and each value keeps that customer's orders in a list. A bare list or set cannot express the grouping directly.

hints: The report performs two operations: lookup by id and ordered storage.
One structure should map a key to a collection.
Use a Map whose values are Lists.

steps.title: Map operations and collection behavior

statements.label: Map.merge can insert or combine a value in one call.
Collectors.groupingBy can build a map of lists from a stream.

steps.explanation: Map.merge and groupingBy build grouped results. HashMap has no iteration-order guarantee; LinkedHashMap does. Map.of is immutable.
hints: HashMap is about lookup, not order.
Map.of rejects structural changes after creation.
